steps.intro: \(n\) = number of sides. There really aren't many rules.

Formula
Remember
rows: the second form is on the formula sheet

tips: Regular = all sides AND all angles equal.
Regular ⇒ fits in a circle — but fitting in a circle does not make it regular.
Forgot an angle? Central angle \(\frac{360°}{n}\), then complete to \(180°\).
A concave polygon (one angle bigger than \(180°\)) still has the angle sum \(180°(n-2)\).

steps.stem:
In pentagon ABCDE, angles B, C and E are right angles, and AB is parallel to CD. Given:
\(\begin{cases} AB=BC=AE=15 \text{ cm} \\ DE=8 \text{ cm} \end{cases}\)
What is the area of the pentagon (in cm²)?
explanation: Draw \(AD\). Triangle \(AED\) has a right angle at \(E\) and legs \(15\) and \(8\). Its area is \(\frac{15\cdot8}{2}=60\), and \(AD=17\) (the 8-15-17 triple).
Drop the height \(AH\) to \(CD\). \(ABCH\) is a square with side \(15\). Its area is \(15^2=225\).
Triangle \(AHD\) has hypotenuse \(AD=17\) and leg \(AH=15\), so \(DH=8\). Its area is \(\frac{15\cdot8}{2}=60\).

steps.stem: A regular hexagon has side length 12 cm. What is its area (in cm²)?
explanation: The three long diagonals split the hexagon into 6 equilateral triangles with side \(12\).
One triangle: \(\frac{12^2\sqrt3}{4}=\frac{144\sqrt3}{4}=36\sqrt3\).
Six triangles: \(6\cdot36\sqrt3=216\sqrt3\).

steps.stem: A regular octagon has side length 10 cm. What is its area (in cm²)?
explanation: Split the octagon: a square in the middle, 4 rectangles and 4 corner right isosceles triangles.
Each corner triangle has hypotenuse \(10\), so its legs are \(\frac{10}{\sqrt2}=5\sqrt2\). Its area is \(\frac12\cdot5\sqrt2\cdot5\sqrt2=25\). Four triangles: \(100\).
Each rectangle: \(10\cdot5\sqrt2=50\sqrt2\). Four rectangles: \(200\sqrt2\).

steps.stem: PQRST is a regular pentagon. What is the size of angle PSQ (marked \(x\) in the figure)?
explanation: Each angle of a regular pentagon is \(\frac{540°}{5}=108°\).
Triangle \(QRS\) is isosceles (\(RQ=RS\)) with vertex angle \(108°\), so \(\angle QSR=\frac{180°-108°}{2}=36°\). In the same way, \(\angle TSP=36°\).

steps.stem: A regular 9-sided polygon ABCDEFGHI is inscribed in a circle with center O and radius r. Which of the following statements is not true?
choices: The circumference of the circle is greater than the perimeter of the polygon.
The perimeter of the polygon is \(9r\).
explanation: Statement 2 is true: every central angle is \(\frac{360°}{9}=40°\).
Statement 1 is true: each arc is longer than its chord (the side), so the circumference is greater than the perimeter.
Statement 4 is true: triangles \(OBC\) and \(OCD\) have three pairs of equal sides, so they are congruent and \(\angle BCO=\angle OCD\).
Statement 3 is false: triangle \(OCD\) has the angles \(40°\), \(70°\) and \(70°\). The side \(CD\) faces \(40°\) and a radius faces \(70°\), so \(CD<r\) and the perimeter is less than \(9r\).

steps.stem: ABCDEF is a regular hexagon. The perimeter of triangle ACE is 42 cm. What is the perimeter of the hexagon (in cm)?
explanation: The three corner triangles are congruent, so triangle \(ACE\) is equilateral: \(AC=\frac{42}{3}=14\).
Triangle \(ABC\) is isosceles with vertex angle \(120°\). The height from \(B\) splits \(AC\) into \(7\) and \(7\) and makes two 30-60-90 triangles.
In each one the long leg is \(7\), so the short leg is \(\frac{7}{\sqrt3}\) and the hypotenuse is \(AB=\frac{14}{\sqrt3}\).
Perimeter: \(6\cdot\frac{14}{\sqrt3}=\frac{84}{\sqrt3}=28\sqrt3\).

steps.title: Regular polygons — facts to know
steps.intro: The shapes the exam loves, and the partitions that solve them fast.
tips: Corner triangle area \(=\frac{a^2\sqrt3}{4}\) — same as an equilateral triangle with the hexagon side \(a\).
Every extra side adds \(180°\) to the angle sum.
Regular polygon: a radius to a vertex bisects its angle; the diagonals from one vertex split it into equal pieces.
Octagon: square + 4 rectangles + 4 silver triangles (together = the square).

steps.stem: ABCDEF is a regular hexagon of side 10 cm. What is the sum of the areas of triangles ABC, CDE and EFA (in cm²)?
explanation: Each corner triangle (\(ABC\), \(CDE\), \(EFA\)) is \(\frac16\) of the hexagon: the same area as an equilateral triangle with side \(10\), \(\frac{10^2\sqrt3}{4}=25\sqrt3\).
Three triangles: \(3\cdot25\sqrt3=75\sqrt3\) (half of the hexagon, \(150\sqrt3\)).

steps.stem: Five squares are constructed externally on five sides of a regular hexagon. Ella claims that the sum of the five square perimeters is 3 times the hexagon perimeter. Adam claims that the sum of the five square areas is greater than the hexagon area. Which of the following is true?
explanation: Plug in a number: side \(=1\).
Ella: the five squares have perimeter \(5\cdot4=20\). The hexagon has perimeter \(6\cdot1=6\), and \(3\cdot6=18\ne20\). Ella is wrong.
Adam: the five squares have area \(5\cdot1=5\). The hexagon has area \(6\cdot\frac{1^2\sqrt3}{4}=\frac{3\sqrt3}{2}<\frac{3\cdot2}{2}=3<5\). Adam is right.
Only Adam is correct.

steps.stem: The accompanying figure shows a regular octagon. KL and MN are perpendicular and intersect at T. K, L, M and N are vertices of the octagon, as shown in the figure. Sara claims that \(LT>2KT\). Ben claims that the perimeter of triangle KMT equals MN. Which of the following is true?
explanation: Let \(KT=MT=1\). Triangle \(KMT\) is right isosceles, so \(KM=\sqrt2\). All the octagon sides are \(\sqrt2\).
Sara: \(LT=\sqrt2+1\approx2.4\) and \(2KT=2\). \(LT>2KT\), so Sara is correct.
Ben: the perimeter of \(KMT\) is \(1+1+\sqrt2=2+\sqrt2\), and \(MN=1+\sqrt2+1=2+\sqrt2\). They are equal, so Ben is correct.
Both are correct.

steps.stem: The accompanying figure shows a regular octagon divided by two vertical segments. The central white rectangle has area \(12+12\sqrt2\) cm². What is the sum of the shaded areas (in cm²)?
explanation: Split the octagon the standard way: a middle square, 4 congruent rectangles and 4 corner triangles. The 4 triangles together equal the middle square.
White: the middle square \(+\) 2 rectangles.
Shaded: 4 triangles \(+\) 2 rectangles \(=\) (the middle square) \(+\) 2 rectangles.
The shaded area equals the white area: \(12+12\sqrt2\).

steps.stem: The sum of the interior angles of a polygon is 1,440°. How many sides does it have?
explanation: Or use an anchor: the octagon has \(1080°\). Each extra side adds \(180°\): \(1260°\) (9 sides), \(1440°\) (10 sides).

steps.stem: A is the sum of the interior angles of a 14-sided polygon, and B is the sum of the interior angles of a 20-sided polygon. The difference \(B-A\) equals the sum of the interior angles of which polygon?
explanation: Faster: 20 sides is 6 sides more than 14, and each side adds \(180°\): \(6\cdot180°=1080°\). (A hexagon is the trap: 6 is the number of extra sides, not the answer.)

steps.stem: Each interior angle of a regular polygon is \(160°\). How many sides does the polygon have?
explanation: Exterior angle: \(180°-160°=20°\).
The exterior angles add up to \(360°\), so \(n=\frac{360°}{20°}=18\).

steps.stem: From one vertex of a polygon, exactly 7 diagonals can be drawn. How many diagonals does the polygon have in all?
explanation: From one vertex there are \(n-3\) diagonals (not to the vertex itself and not to its two neighbors). \(n-3=7\), so \(n=10\).
Each of the 10 vertices sends 7 diagonals: \(10\cdot7=70\). Each diagonal has two ends, so it was counted twice.
In all: \(\frac{10\cdot7}{2}=35\).

steps.title: Polygons meeting at a point
steps.intro: Two steps: 360° around the point, then the isosceles triangle.

head: Situation
Rule
rows: !Two regular polygons on a common side
Their free sides at the shared vertex
both equal the common side \(\rightarrow\) isosceles triangle
their angles add up to exactly \(360°\)

tips: Know the angles: triangle \(60°\), square \(90°\), pentagon \(108°\), hexagon \(120°\), octagon \(135°\).
Square + pentagon on a common side: gap \(360°-90°-108°=162°\).

steps.stem: Square ABCD and regular pentagon ABEFG share the side AB. They lie on opposite sides of AB, as shown in the figure. What is the size of angle ADG?
explanation: At \(A\) three angles fill the full turn: the square's \(90°\), the pentagon's \(108°\) and \(\angle DAG\).
\(AD=AB\) (square) and \(AG=AB\) (pentagon), so \(AD=AG\): triangle \(ADG\) is isosceles.

By how many degrees is an interior angle of a regular dodecagon greater than an interior angle of a regular octagon?
explanation: Difference: \(150°-135°=15°\). (Or with exterior angles: \(45°-30°=15°\).)

steps.stem: Each exterior angle of a regular polygon is \(24°\). What is the sum of its interior angles?
Two congruent regular octagons share one entire side and lie on opposite sides of it. The perimeter of their combined outer boundary is 70 cm. What is the perimeter of one octagon (in cm)?
explanation: Two octagons have \(2\cdot8=16\) sides. The shared side is inside the shape, so it is counted in neither boundary: the outer boundary has \(16-2=14\) equal sides.
Each side: \(\frac{70}{14}=5\) cm. One octagon: \(8\cdot5=40\) cm.
(\(35\) is the trap: \(\frac{70}{16}\cdot8\) forgets that the shared side is not on the boundary.)

steps.stem: A polygon has 20 diagonals. How many sides does it have?
explanation: Number of diagonals: \(\frac{n(n-3)}{2}=20\), so \(n(n-3)=40\).
Work back from the answers: \(n=8\) gives \(8\cdot5=40\). (The others: \(n=5\) gives \(5\) diagonals, \(n=7\) gives \(\frac{7\cdot4}{2}=14\), \(n=10\) gives \(\frac{10\cdot7}{2}=35\).)
The polygon has 8 sides.

steps.stem: In which of the following polygons do all the diagonals meet at a single point in the interior?
explanation: A trapezoid has only 2 diagonals, and they cross each other inside the shape. So all its diagonals meet at one point.

A regular pentagon has \(\frac{5\cdot2}{2}=5\) diagonals, and they do not all pass through one point. The same is true for the octagon. In the regular hexagon only the 3 long diagonals meet at the center; the 6 short ones do not pass through it.

steps.stem: A regular hexagon has area 96 cm². Three alternating vertices are joined to form a triangle. What is the area of this triangle (in cm²)?
explanation: Each corner triangle is \(\frac16\) of the hexagon, so the three corner triangles together are \(\frac12\) of it.
The triangle in the middle is the other half: \(\frac{96}{2}=48\).

steps.stem: Pentagon ABCDE consists of square BCDE of side 6 cm and triangle ABE. Given: \(AB=AE\) and angle BAE is 90°. What is the pentagon’s perimeter (in cm)?
explanation: \(BE=6\) is the hypotenuse of the right isosceles triangle \(ABE\), so \(AB=AE=\frac{6}{\sqrt2}=3\sqrt2\).
The boundary has three square sides and two roof sides: \(3\cdot6+2\cdot3\sqrt2=18+6\sqrt2\).

explanation: Each hexagon angle is \(120°\), so the angle next to it on line \(CD\) is \(180°-120°=60°\).

steps.stem: Polygon K has \(a+2\) sides and polygon L has \(b+5\) sides. a and b are whole numbers, \(b\ge3\) and \(a>b+3\). By how much is the interior-angle sum of K greater than that of L?
explanation: Faster: \(K\) has \((a+2)-(b+5)=a-b-3\) more sides, and each side adds \(180°\).

steps.stem: A convex polygon is inscribed in a circle. Its sides divide the circle into 13 separate regions, including the polygon’s interior. How many sides does the polygon have?
explanation: Each side cuts off one region between the side and the circle: \(n\) regions. The inside of the polygon is one more region.

steps.stem: A regular octagon has side length 8 cm. The central square and the four adjoining rectangles in its standard partition are shaded. What is the total shaded area (in cm²)?
explanation: Each rectangle has sides \(8\) and \(\frac{8}{\sqrt2}=4\sqrt2\), so its area is \(8\cdot4\sqrt2=32\sqrt2\). Four rectangles: \(128\sqrt2\).
Shaded: \(64+128\sqrt2\).

\(\begin{cases} \alpha=\angle STU \\ \beta=\angle PQV \end{cases}\)
What is \(\alpha-\beta\)?
explanation: \(\alpha\) is an angle of the octagon: \(\alpha=180°-\frac{360°}{8}=135°\).

steps.stem: Six congruent rhombi meet at a common vertex and fill a full turn, with equal angles at that vertex. Each rhombus has perimeter 28 cm. The diagonals joining consecutive outer endpoints form the inner hexagon shown in the accompanying figure. What is its perimeter (in cm)?
explanation: The 6 equal angles at the common vertex fill \(360°\), so each is \(\frac{360°}{6}=60°\).
Each rhombus side is \(\frac{28}{4}=7\).
Each rhombus is made of two triangles with two sides \(7\) and a \(60°\) angle between them: equilateral triangles. So its short diagonal (a side of the inner hexagon) is \(7\).
Perimeter: \(6\cdot7=42\).

steps.stem: KLMNPQ is a regular hexagon inscribed in a circle. The tangent at Q meets the extension of LK beyond K at S. What is angle KSQ?
explanation: \(\angle SKQ\) is next to the hexagon angle \(\angle LKQ=120°\) on line \(LS\), so \(\angle SKQ=180°-120°=60°\).
Let \(O\) be the center. A radius is perpendicular to the tangent: \(\angle OQS=90°\).
Triangle \(OKQ\) is equilateral (in a regular hexagon the side equals the radius), so \(\angle OQK=60°\) and \(\angle KQS=90°-60°=30°\).
In triangle \(KSQ\): \(\angle KSQ=180°-60°-30°=90°\).

Pentagon ABCDE consists of rectangle BCDE and isosceles triangle ABE. Given:
\(\begin{cases} AB=AE=6a \\ BC=2a \\ \angle BAE=120° \end{cases}\)
What is the area of the pentagon?
explanation: Draw the height from \(A\) to \(BE\). It splits triangle \(ABE\) into two 30-60-90 triangles with hypotenuse \(6a\).
The height (short leg) is \(3a\). Half of \(BE\) (long leg) is \(3a\sqrt3\), so \(BE=6a\sqrt3\).
Triangle: \(\frac{6a\sqrt3\cdot3a}{2}=9\sqrt3\,a^2\). Rectangle: \(6a\sqrt3\cdot2a=12\sqrt3\,a^2\).
Total: \(21\sqrt3\,a^2\).

steps.stem: A regular hexagon is inscribed in a circle. Its six short diagonals are tangent to a smaller circle with the same center. What is the ratio of the area of the larger circle to the area of the smaller circle?
explanation: Let the large radius be \(R\). Take a short diagonal, like \(BF\). Triangle \(OBF\) is isosceles with \(OB=OF=R\) and \(\angle BOF=2\cdot60°=120°\).
The perpendicular from \(O\) to \(BF\) splits it into two 30-60-90 triangles with hypotenuse \(R\). The small radius is the short leg: \(\frac{R}{2}\).
The radii are in the ratio \(2:1\), so the areas are in the ratio \(2^2:1^2=4:1\).

steps.stem: A regular octagon is divided into eight congruent triangles by joining its center to its vertices. On every other side, a congruent triangle is constructed externally. What is the outside angle α in the accompanying figure between one attached triangle and the adjacent octagon side?
explanation: The octagon angle is \(180°-\frac{360°}{8}=135°\).
Each central triangle has head angle \(\frac{360°}{8}=45°\) and base angles \(\frac{180°-45°}{2}=67.5°\). The attached triangle is congruent, so its angle at the marked vertex is \(67.5°\).
Around the vertex: \(\alpha=360°-135°-67.5°=157.5°\).

steps.stem: The accompanying figure shows six congruent regular hexagons surrounding a hexagonal opening. What is the ratio of the length of the outer boundary of the arrangement to the sum of the perimeters of the six hexagons? (Do not include the boundary of the central opening.)
explanation: Each hexagon has 6 sides. It shares 1 side with the opening and 1 side with each of its two neighbors, so 3 of its sides are on the outer boundary.
Outer boundary: \(6\cdot3=18\) sides. The six perimeters: \(6\cdot6=36\) sides.
The ratio is \(\frac{18}{36}=\frac12\).

steps.stem: Eight congruent circles of radius 3 cm have centers at the vertices of a regular octagon. Each circle is externally tangent to its two neighbors. What is the sum of the areas of the parts of the circles lying outside the octagon (in cm²)?
explanation: The octagon angle is \(135°\), so at each vertex \(\frac{135}{360}=\frac38\) of the circle is inside the octagon and \(\frac58\) is outside.
Each circle: \(\pi\cdot3^2=9\pi\). The part outside: \(\frac58\cdot9\pi=\frac{45}{8}\pi\).
Eight circles: \(8\cdot\frac{45}{8}\pi=45\pi\).
